- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) or neutral (0.3–0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the following 5–7 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction.
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 3–5 days of a new sentiment shift; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for early periods.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 2+ consecutive 0.5–0.7 sentiment swings), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to catch momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period spikes (last 5–7 days of true outcome); increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
